verdicts.reason: I checked this against the held official FR texts. Every quote matches its held span exactly (kit check and claim-checker pass, 265/265 quotes exact; checker output was reverted afterwards and the cache deleted). The ending actor is EO 11490 sec. 3015 item (3), 'Executive Order No. 10312 of December 10,1951', on PDF page 95 of FR-1969-10-30. The order has no effective-date wording, so it took effect on signing, 1969-10-28. All 12 clauses carry that date and actor. The inventory runs from Sec. 1 to Sec. 8 with no gap or overlap. Sec. 3014 is limited by 'Except as provided in Section 3015'. The Part 18 quote is verbatim. D6: EO 10438 sec. 1(b), EO 10773 sec. 4(b)(3), EO 10782 and EO 11051 sec. 601(2)/604(4),(9) are verified as reference or officer changes, not ends. EO 11092 sec. 9 does not derogate. No held order names 10312 between 1962 and 1969. Savings state transferred_or_accrued is supported. Observations, none changing the outcome: (1) the OFR 'See' edge on EO 10705 pointing to 10312 (EDGES LE-24484b14ccc8) is not discussed. EO 10705 sec. 3 says it does not terminate or modify other orders, and its amend/revoke authority applies only after a war proclamation, so it ends nothing. (2) The 1968 statutory rename of the Office of Emergency Planning to the Office of Emergency Preparedness is not mentioned. (3) The by-number scan list leaves out page-number hits (EO 13825, 9468, 9601).

No savings clause exists for revoked orders, and transferred_or_accrued is supported. No pending owner ruling (report deadline, transcription-as-copy, strike-and-reinsert) is implicated.

It contradicts the claim's own whole_order_end.mechanism ('took effect on signing, October 28, 1969'), all 12 clause first_end dates (1969-10-28), the research_rationale ('effective on signing 1969-10-28') and the held official text (The White House, October 28, 1969; F.R. Doc. 69-13005 filed Oct. 28, 1969). kit.py check and the claim-checker both fail it with whole_order_end_not_last_clause_end. (2) The rationale records an OFR 'See' note to FR Doc. 62-9459, 27 FR 9418, as 'not held, requested in FETCH_QUEUE' (FETCH_QUEUE line 573), yet unresolved_material_gaps is []. Either list the unread document as a gap or read it before claiming no gaps. Defects: (1) D6 is incomplete. The Department of Transportation Act (Pub. L. 89-670, effective 1967-04-01) moved the Federal Aviation Agency into DOT as the Federal Aviation Administration and transferred its functions. That is a candidate earlier change or end of an order whose every clause assigns duties to the 'Administrator of the Federal Aviation Agency'. The claim admits the statute 'is not held and was not read' and dismisses the question by assumption. It attaches no later event, which is inconsistent with how this batch attached the analogous officer transfers (EO 10438 and others) on EO 10312 and EO 10346. (2) The held EO 11382 of 1967-11-28 (amending Executive orders for DOT functions; sec. 15 Prior actions; sec. 16 Revocations) is not discussed. It does not name EO 11003, which supports 'no amendment', but the D6 record must cite it. (3) An OFR 'See' note to FR Doc. 63-3328, 28 FR 3125, is 'not held, requested in FETCH_QUEUE' (line 574), yet unresolved_material_gaps is []. Admitted unread material contradicts the empty gap list.
